verdict.rationale: Jules runs tasks asynchronously in a cloud VM and notifies you on completion. Tasks can be triggered by a GitHub issue label or through the API, which supports automating bug fixing and code reviews, with optional automatic PR creation and optional plan approval. These are one-off, triggered background tasks, not a documented, user-configurable recurring automation or schedule. Community comments about babysitting and loops do not concretely contradict the background-execution capability. Missing for 10: native recurring/scheduled automation setup, documented end-to-end autonomous pipelines beyond per-task API calls, independent corroboration of unattended automation runs.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Jules runs in a virtual machine where it clones your code, installs dependencies, and modifies files.
You’ll be notified when the task completes or needs your input.
You can use the API to create custom workflows, automate tasks like bug fixing and code reviews
Use the "jules" label in an issue to assign a task directly in GitHub.
The `automationMode` field is optional. By default, no PR will be automatically created.
